transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 09:30 PT — Duration ~45m
Attendees: Maya, Priya, Liam, Jordan, Samir, Ava

Summary: quick weekly sync between IT, Finance, and Security to align on Okta SSO migration timeline, KMS billing reallocation for new HSM cluster, SOC 2 readiness items, and VPC peering for upcoming private deployments. Some background noise / transcription glitches noted.

[00:00] Maya: Okay, good morning everyone, should we get started? We've got 45 minutes on this — thanks for making time.
[00:07] Priya: morning, yeah, quick note on finance side, got the March close, so I have a tighter window to move funds for the KMS/HSM purchase if we decide to go ahead.
[00:15] Liam: uh-huh, and from security perspective, we need the service accounts list for SSO mapping, also the SOC two — sorry, SOC 2 prep — auditor asked for preliminary list of assets and key managers.
[00:27] Jordan: just to flag, the VPC peering for private deployments is being requested by two enterprise customers for Dedicated, so if we don't have IP ranges locked down that will block onboarding.
[00:35] Maya: right, so agenda: 1) SSO migration (Okta), 2) KMS/HSM billing & budget, 3) SOC2 readiness, 4) VPC peering / network, 5) procurement timing. anyone want to add?
[00:45] Ava: maybe add the sticky point about audit logs retention, there's been a lot of asks from product for longer retention but that bumps cost.
[00:52] Maya: good call, add that.

---
[05:10] SSO / Okta migration
[05:12] Maya: quick status — engineering finished the Okta test connector last week, we did a smoke test with a small group, some mappings are off — groups aren't syncing for service accounts. so need the final list.
[05:25] Liam: yeah the service account names get munged in the provisioning. transcription note: sometimes service acc reads as "service ack" in our logs, so double-check.
[05:33] Priya: do we have an ETA to cutover? finance needs to know when provisioning will create new SSO-linked users vs legacy invites for billing access.
[05:40] Jordan: technically we can cutover next week but we need the mapping and the list of owners to approve auto-joins.
[05:46] Maya: action: I'll send the access matrix by Friday with owners. Priya, will that timing work for finance?
[05:52] Priya: yes, if you send by Friday I can update the cost center allocation for the new service accounts before the invoice.

[10:00] KMS / HSM billing & budget
[10:03] Priya: so the quote for the HSM-backed KMS came in higher than expected — partly licensing and partly the key-splitting we need for multi-region. We can either absorb into existing security budget or move funds from the infra reserve.
[10:18] Maya: what's the delta? numbers.
[10:20] Priya: roughly $35k upfront and $6k/month additional; one-time is for onboarding and HSM cluster setup.
[10:28] Liam: security justification: having HSM reduces the attestation burden for SOC2 and for enterprise customers who require HSM. also key rotation policy is easier to enforce with KMS integrated.
[10:36] Samir: from legal side, customers often ask for KMS control statements in contracts; having the HSM is a commercial plus. but we need to be precise about who has key access and the logs.
[10:44] Maya: ok, Priya can you put a recommendation in writing with options: (A) absorb into security FY26 budget, (B) shift infra reserve and amortize over 12 months, (C) postpone and use cloud-managed KMS with less attestation.
[10:55] Priya: will do, I'll send by Tuesday.

[15:00] SOC 2 readiness / external auditor
[15:05] Liam: quick update — the external auditor asked for scoping information; they want a list of infra assets, key management, SSO config, and evidence of privileged access reviews. I started a gap checklist but it's rough.
[15:20] Maya: do we have retention windows for logs documented? Ava, you mentioned product wants longer retention — what's the ask?
[15:26] Ava: product asked for 12 months in the analytics plane, but security policy recommends 90 days for the raw audit logs to keep costs down. We can tier older logs into cold storage but access is slower.
[15:38] Priya: there's a cost delta there too — long retention is about $8k/mo for hot storage, cold is much cheaper but retrieval costs apply.
[15:45] Samir: auditor will accept tiered retention if the policy and access controls are documented; just need the runbook and retention SLA.
[15:52] Liam: action: I'll finish the gap checklist and share a short slide deck for the auditor by next week.

[22:10] VPC peering / private deployments
[22:13] Jordan: two customers want direct VPC peering for private deployments; current default is VPN with NAT which is fine, but peering requires IP range assignments and a standard peering template. Also need firewall rules and BGP routes.
[22:27] Maya: are there any blockers from security? Liam?
[22:30] Liam: main issue is isolation — peering can introduce lateral risk if config is wrong. we need strict route tables and no cross-tenant route advertisements. Also logging at the peering level.
[22:40] Jordan: propose we standardize a /22 allocation per customer and share a Terraform module — I can prepare that and include example security groups.
[22:48] Priya: procurement will need lead time — 2-3 weeks after design sign-off. Invoicing for Dedicated capacity needs the PO in that window.

[28:00] Procurement & timing for Dedicated capacity
[28:05] Priya: reminder, for Dedicated PO we need legal approval of terms (Samir), budget sign off (Maya/Priya), and final capacity numbers from sales. If sales pushes to start in April we need to have PO by mid-March.
[28:18] Samir: I'll draft procurement clause that ties SLA credits and termination terms to the PO and share with Priya by EOD next Thursday.
[28:26] Maya: any dependencies on SOC2 completion for starting Dedicated? Sales is pushing but some customers ask for SOC2 in place before production.
[28:36] Liam: we can start onboarding with minimal controls but flag as pre-SOC2; some customers will accept that with appropriate contractual language.

[33:10] Misc notes / glitches in transcription
[33:12] Maya: note — the transcript sometimes turns KV cache into KV cash and "Okta" became "Oakta" in the auto transcript; ignore those and cross-check the doc.
[33:20] Priya: also the finance code "CC-Infra" was read in the transcript as "see see infra" so apologies for any confusion.

[35:00] Recap & next steps
[35:05] Maya: quick recap — Liam finish SOC2 gap checklist; Jordan share VPC peering Terraform + diagram; Priya confirm KMS budget options; Samir draft procurement clause; I'll send SSO access matrix. We reconvene next Tuesday if needed.
[35:25] Samir: noted.
[35:28] Priya: will follow up on budget fast.
[35:30] Liam: I'll ping the auditor to lock a 3/15 slot.
[35:35] Maya: great, thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

References: SSO migration checklist (link: internal:/docs/okta-migration), KMS quote (link: internal:/finance/kms-quote-2026-03), VPC peering draft (link: internal:/infra/vpc-peering-draft).
